name: Cooper Monaco Type 61P Maserati
description:
The Cooper Monaco Type 61P Maserati is a fascinating hybrid of British chassis engineering and Italian power. The Type 61, also known as the "Monaco" due to its enclosed bodywork, was Cooper's answer to the demand for a sports racing car that could compete in both open and closed-cockpit categories during the early 1960s.

This particular example represents a popular privateer modification: fitting the robust Cooper Monaco chassis with Maserati's magnificent 4.9-liter DOHC V8 engine. The Maserati V8, originally developed for the 450S sports racer, was renowned for its smooth power delivery and distinctive exhaust note. In this application, it produces approximately 350 horsepower through a 5-speed gearbox.

The Cooper Monaco's lightweight tubular spaceframe chassis, combined with the torquey Italian V8, created a formidable package for Group 4 racing. Weighing just 745 kg with driver and fuel, the car offered an excellent power-to-weight ratio that made it competitive against purpose-built prototypes from larger manufacturers.

Cars like this Type 61P exemplify the creative spirit of 1960s sports car racing, where privateers often achieved competitive results by combining the best elements from different manufacturers. The marriage of Cooper's nimble chassis with Maserati's muscular V8 produced a car that was both fast and reliable in the hands of gentleman racers competing in the World Sportscar Championship.
